The series is trend‑dominated with moderate ranking stability – a DBA (dynamic Bayesian averaging) may adapt to shifting model strengths.
test a different weighted approach using softmax_neg_error to see if a softer weighting improves over inverse_error in this trend‑dominated, moderately stable series.
test a weighted combination on the selected top‑7 pool using inverse error to see if restricting to strong models improves over full‑pool weighted.
The series has moderate ranking stability and strong trend; a trimmed mean may reduce influence of outlier models.

I will test a weighted combination that uses the softmax_neg_error weighting on the already-selected pool4, to see if a more aggressive weighting improves over the inverse_error on pool4. This explores a different weighting method while keeping the same model subset.
The series is trend‑dominated with moderate ranking stability; a simple robust aggregator like median may perform well and is a different strategy type from weighted.
The series has moderate ranking stability and a strong trend; a forward selection weight may capture complementary models better than simple inverse error.
Test a dynamic Bayesian averaging on the strong pool4 to see if adapting weights per window improves over static weighted combos.
test a simple mean on the strong pool4 to see if reducing weighting complexity helps given the trend-dominated regime.
The series is trend-dominated with moderate ranking stability; exploring a per-horizon weighted combination may capture subtle horizon shifts that a static weighted pool missed.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool4 weighted by w4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.4302. Series context: trend strength 0.9559 and seasonal strength 0.0922; model ranking is moderate across windows (Kendall tau 0.423); 5 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 15.258.
